# R330 — Actual persistent serve route: no-MTP, `--spec 4`, GEN16 versus GEN128

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source audit on W HEAD `e3c904e2`, plus prior report/registry review. No tests, build, imported project code, model/GPU/process/profiler work, Git operation, cleanup, active-record reads, or source edits. Main alone measures. This report adds no measurement and leaves R329/R322/R323 unchanged.

## Finding

R329's remaining-output verifier-window explanation cited the standalone generation loop at `generate.cpp:10900`; it does not describe the ordinary persistent `--serve` loop assigned here. In the actual `--serve`, batch-off, no-MTP route with `--spec 4`, suffix drafting off and lookup chain off, each serial `Verifier::run` is called with `T=1` for every generated token, including all first 16 tokens. The serve loop passes the request's remaining output budget to `verifier_window`, but with `requested=1` and at least one output left, that function returns one. Thus GEN16 and GEN128 have the same verifier row count and same generation-control path through the first 16 outputs, conditional on the same initial request/session state and same model/runtime settings. `--max_new` cannot make earlier serve windows multi-row or shorten a terminal window before output 16 in this recipe.

The cap still changes admission and when generation stops. GEN16 terminates after output 16; GEN128 continues. It can also change the capacity reserved for the host `consumed` vector (`n + max_new + S` at `:9212`), but this is host bookkeeping and does not change the `T` argument, verify graph shape, or logits math for the first 16 calls. With prompt length 32,768, context 262,144 and fixed `--no-kv-grow`, both output limits pass context admission; no elastic K/V growth is in play. The source finding does not prove equal wall time or output quality: other request state, runtime scheduling, device/CPU contention, and run variation are outside this route proof. Matching output IDs or LP observations are not a quality conclusion.

## Exact serve control flow

The persistent serve setup computes `use_mtp = !o.mtp.empty()` at `generate.cpp:5763`. The server takes the `GEN <max_new> ...` value as a per-request local at `:8121`; `context_bounds::admission` checks prompt plus requested output extent against the fixed context at `:8282-8285`. The serving loop establishes `S = o.spec` and `S_mtp = ...` at `:7208-7213`. This makes `S` and the verifier's allocated window buffers four for `--spec 4`; it does not by itself make actual serial `T` four when MTP is absent.

After prompt handling, the serial request path starts at the final prompt token (`:9183-9185`). It loops while `produced_n < max_new` (`:9781`). In each iteration the initial request size is explicitly `use_mtp ? min(S_mtp, 1 + mtp_candidates) : 1` (`:9782`); `first_window` also forces 1 (`:9787`). The only non-MTP ways to raise that requested `T` here are suffix drafts (`:9792-9798`) and `--lookup-chain` (`:9802-9813`), both disabled in the assigned recipe. Hence `T=1`, `chain_n=0` for every iteration.

The serve call then applies `verifier_window(o.max_context, p, T + chain_n, max_new - produced_n)` (`:9815-9819`). Its implementation returns the minimum of `requested`, context cells remaining and outputs remaining, or zero for invalid bounds (`include/strata/core/context_bounds.hpp:25-28`). For output index k in 0..15, the loop begins with `produced_n=k`, so GEN16 has remaining budget `16-k` (1 at k=15) and GEN128 has `128-k`; both are at least 1. Given context headroom, both therefore call `verifier_window(..., requested=1, outputs>=1)`, yielding `T=1`. The actual caller is `ver.run(T, window.data(), p, win_pool_fn, win_pool_user, outv.data(), err)` (`generate.cpp:9856`).

With `T=1`, `a` starts at zero and its match loop cannot advance (`:9860-9861`), commit consumes exactly one row (`:9879`), and the emission loop writes exactly one token if not stopped (`:9899-9900`). The first window is a one-row window in both lengths; `first_window` is then cleared (`:9897`). For each subsequent first-16 token the same one-row logic repeats. After each emission, the no-MTP expression `!use_mtp || ...` short-circuits to success without calling `mtp.draft` (`:9934-9938`). Thus no draft computation depends on whether `produced_n` equals the short cap; the next loop iteration runs for GEN128, while GEN16 exits at the loop condition.

## Applicability limits

This conclusion requires the exact route constraints: persistent `--serve`; batch disabled; no loaded `--mtp`; `--spec 4` only as window capacity; `--suffix-draft 0`; `--lookup-chain 0`; same initial session/prompt state; and enough context capacity. If MTP is loaded, its candidate count can make `T>1`, and remaining output can clip a window near the cap. If suffix or lookup-chain drafting is enabled without MTP, those facilities can also request multi-token windows and make the output budget relevant to window shape. Batch and pipeline branches have their own T-selection/commit logic and are outside this finding.

`--max_new` changes the accepted-request boundary (`:8282-8285`) and loop exit, not the first 16 `Verifier::run` dimensions in this no-draft serial recipe. Even so, two GEN requests on a persistent server need a genuinely equal starting state to make a clean comparison: request-cache/checkpoint reuse, prior requests, learned process state, and host/device scheduling can differ. This source audit cannot establish that such state was equal in any measured pair. It also cannot conclude equal per-token wall time, numerical distributions, task quality, or correctness from the call shape alone.

R322 already corrected the earlier standalone/serve route attribution for persistent Prefill lifecycle. R323 explains a synchronization distinction between standalone fixed-history and serve; its fixed-history mechanism is not needed to determine this no-draft T=1 result. R329's standalone citation `generate.cpp:10900-10907` remains valid for its one-shot route only and should not be applied to this serve path. The report registry v176 was reviewed for context; it reports 836 completed entries and does not list R322/R323/R329 as new entries. No earlier report or receipt was modified.
